title: PowerPoint on Windows: Copilot agent notifies you when work finishes or needs attention
summary: The briefing accurately reports the roadmap plan and distinguishes it from documentation for the separately described PowerPoint Agents. The cited administrative paths and licensing command are supported; targeted searches found no published notification-specific controls, default, entitlement or meter.

claims.claim: The listed Microsoft 365 admin center path reaches Disable Anthropic as a Microsoft subprocessor.
claims.quote: select Copilot > Settings. On the User access page, select AI providers operating as Microsoft subprocessors. On the AI providers operating as Microsoft subprocessors page, under Available subprocessors for your organization, select Disable Anthropic as a Microsoft subprocessor.

claims.claim: No documented automation operation was found for disabling Anthropic as a Microsoft subprocessor.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Graph AI providers Anthropic subprocessor disable settings API PowerShell. Read connect-to-ai-subprocessor and returned AI-provider access, model-availability, Graph and PowerShell excerpts; none supplies an operation setting this control.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center > Users > Active users > user > Licenses and Apps > Licenses reaches the user's licence control.
claims.quote: go to the Users > Active users page. Select the row of the user that you want to assign a license to. In the right pane, select Licenses and Apps. Expand the Licenses section, select the boxes for the licenses that you want to assign

claims.claim: Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @() assigns the specified licence using Microsoft Graph PowerShell.

claims.claim: User Administrator is a minimum role sufficient to assign user licences.
